Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated sushi spots around Los Angeles—based on Michelin ratings, food‑critic praise, and crowd favorites: | Restaurant | Location | Highlights | |------------|----------|-------------| | **Nobu** – *Beverly Hills* & *West Hollywood* | • Fusion of Japanese classics + Peruvian flair
• Consistently high‑rated “sushi” dishes (e.g., toro sashimi)
• Upscale vibe, great for special occasions | | **Sushi Gen** – *Little Tokyo* | • Classic Edomae-style nigiri from seasoned chef Kenji Saito
• Freshest fish daily, often sourced directly from Japan
• Intimate setting, perfect for purists | | **Kazuya** – *Hollywood* | • Chef Kazuya Takahashi brings authentic Edo‑style techniques
• Known for its omakase tasting menu featuring seasonal catches
• Cozy yet refined atmosphere | | **Sugarfish** – *Multiple locations* *(Note: as of early 2025 many branches have shuttered)* | • Focuses on simplicity and quality over gimmicks
• Great for casual dining and takeout
• Still popular where it remains open | | **Matsuri** – *Downtown LA* | • Contemporary twist on traditional rolls
• Creative fusion plates (think miso‑marinated ahi tuna tartare)
• Trendy spot favored by younger crowds | ### Quick Tips If You’re Looking To Book: 1. **Reserve Early:** Especially for omakase menus at Nobu or Matsuri—they fill up fast. 2. **Ask About Seasonal Menus:** Many chefs change their offerings weekly depending on what arrives fresh. 3. **Check Current Status:** Some restaurants may close temporarily due to renovations or staffing changes. If you’d like more tailored recommendations—for example, budget ranges, specific neighborhoods, or dietary restrictions—just let me know!
